The kernel of A . B is Integral A(x, u) B(u, y) and Tr(A . B) = Integral A(x, y) B(y, x). FunctionalDerivative differentiates it (δ Tr ln A = Tr(A^-1 δA)); ExpandTrace expands it around a bare propagator; ZeroDimensionalValue evaluates it in zero dimensions.

nodes.name: OperatorTrace
nodes.usage: OperatorTrace[A] is the trace Tr A of an operator A (see TraceLog); OperatorTrace[1] is the trace of the identity. ExpandTrace writes the trace of a product of kernels as a ring of diagrams.

nodes.name: OperatorKernel
nodes.usage: OperatorKernel[A][x, y] is the kernel A(x, y) of an operator A that is not a single kernel, e.g. OperatorKernel[G^-1][x, y] = G^-1(x, y) (symmetric when G is). ExpandTrace writes it as diagrams and contracts Integral G^-1(a, u) G(u, b) to δ(a, b).

nodes.name: ExpandTrace
nodes.usage: ExpandTrace[expr] writes the traces (OperatorTrace), kernels (OperatorKernel) and universal functionals (LegendreTransform, as Phi[G] + κ Tr(S . G)) in expr as diagrams, with the products of inverse kernels contracted (Integral G^-1(a, u) G(u, b) du = δ(a, b)), and brings the result to canonical form. ExpandTrace[expr, G0, n] also expands around the bare propagator G0, to n insertions: Tr ln(c (G0^-1 - X)) = Tr ln(c G0^-1) - Sum_k Tr((G0 X)^k)/k (a series of rings) and (c (G0^-1 - X))^-1 = (1/c) Sum_k (G0 X)^k G0 (the Dyson series); a propagator replaced by an operator, e.g. G -> (G0^-1 - S)^-1 with S = LabelFunction[sigma, {a, b}], is expanded in the diagrams too. The option "MaximumOrder" -> {V, m} keeps the terms of order m or less in V (a coupling symbol or the head of the interaction lines), truncating the products as they are formed.

nodes.name: LegendreTransform
nodes.usage: LegendreTransform[Phi, G -> S] is Potthoff's universal functional ℱ[S] = Phi[G[S]] - Tr(S G[S]) (fermions; + 1/2 Tr(S G) for real bosons, "Statistics" -> "Boson", + Tr(S G) for complex bosons), the Legendre transform of the Luttinger-Ward functional Phi from G to the self-energy S: G[S] is the propagator at which SelfEnergy[Phi, G] equals S. It is inert: FunctionalDerivative with respect to S[x, y] gives -G[S](y, x) (fermions; 1/2 G[S], G[S] for bosons), G[S] being LegendrePropagator; with respect to a kernel of Phi other than G, e.g. an interaction V[x, y], it gives δPhi/δV at G = G[S] (ℱ is stationary in G); with respect to G it gives 0. ExpandTrace and ZeroDimensionalValue write it out as Phi[G] - Tr(S . G) (fermions; + 1/2 Tr(S . G) for real bosons, + Tr(S . G) for complex bosons), and G[S] as G. It depends on the interaction only, not on G0: the diagrams of Phi contain only G and the interaction.

nodes.name: LegendrePropagator
nodes.usage: LegendrePropagator[G -> S, {V, ...}][x, y] is G[S](x, y), the propagator at which the self-energy of a Luttinger-Ward functional Phi (of G and of the kernels V, ...) equals S: the stationary point in G of Potthoff's universal functional ℱ[S] = LegendreTransform[Phi, G -> S], whose derivative with respect to S is written with it. It is shown as G[S](x, y), and ExpandTrace and ZeroDimensionalValue write it as G(x, y) (G -> g(S) among the rules of ZeroDimensionalValue). Its derivatives are not available (δG[S]/δS is the inverse of the irreducible vertex, (δΣ/δG)^-1, δG[S]/δV needs it too): FunctionalDerivative gives a message and the terms that need one are $Failed, as are the second derivatives of ℱ and of SelfEnergyFunctional with respect to S.

nodes.name: SelfEnergyFunctional
nodes.usage: SelfEnergyFunctional[Phi, G0 -> S, G] is Potthoff's self-energy functional Ω_G0[S] = ℱ[S] - Tr ln(-(G0^-1 - S)) for fermions (ℱ[S] + 1/2 Tr ln(D0^-1 - S) for real bosons, ℱ[S] + Tr ln(G0^-1 - S) for complex bosons; option "Statistics"), with ℱ = LegendreTransform[Phi, G -> S] the universal functional. G0 enters only through the trace-log (Potthoff writes Ω_t[S]: his t, the one-body part, is what G0^-1 contains besides the frequencies), so that ℱ is the same for every system with the same interaction and can be computed on a simpler reference system (the idea of the variational cluster approximation and of DMFT): Ω_G0[S] is stationary at the physical self-energy, FunctionalDerivative with respect to S[x, y] being (G0^-1 - S)^-1(y, x) - G[S](y, x) (Dyson), and equal to -log Z there. G[S] is (G0^-1 - S)^-1 only at the stationary point: Ω_G0[S] is a Legendre transform, not the substitution G -> (G0^-1 - S)^-1 in Γ[G] (EffectiveAction2PI), which is stationary at the same point but has G0 also inside Phi, and is therefore not universal.

nodes.name: ZeroDimensionalValue
nodes.usage: ZeroDimensionalValue[expr, {G -> g, V -> u, ...}] is the value of expr in zero dimensions (one point, possibly with internal states): integrals dropped, DeltaFunction -> 1, every kernel h[x, y] replaced by its value, and a factor n (option "LoopFactor" -> n, e.g. 2s + 1; default 1) for every closed loop of kernels (ClosedLoopCount; kernels of operators, OperatorKernel[A][x, y], included, so that Integral A(x, y) B(y, x) counts as the trace Tr(A . B)) and every trace: OperatorTrace[A] -> n a and TraceLog[A] -> Log[a^n] (n Log[a] for a symbolic n), a the value of the operator A (products of numbers). LegendreTransform[Phi, G -> S] is written out as Phi[G] - Tr(S . G) for fermions (+ 1/2 Tr(S . G) for real bosons, + Tr(S . G) for complex bosons), with G -> g(S) given among the rules. The option "Loops" -> {G, ...} gives the heads of the lines whose loops are counted (default Automatic: every two-label kernel of expr that is neither symmetric nor an interaction line, i.e. propagators, self-energies and one-body sources, and the kernels of operators made of them). It is the exact check of the weights of the diagrams on a zero-dimensional model whose integral can be done. When a value is a list, an array of rank the number of labels of its kernel (e.g. the 4 x 4 Nambu matrix of one site with spin 1/2, NambuField = (psiUp, psiDn, psibarUp, psibarDn)), the labels run over the internal states: DeltaFunction is the identity, integrals are sums, operators are matrices (numbers times the identity), Tr ln A = Log[Det[A]], Tr A = Tr[A], OperatorKernel[A][x, y] the entry, and "LoopFactor" is not used; "Indices" -> {x -> i, ...} gives the internal states of the free labels.

nodes.name: SuperfieldComponents
nodes.usage: SuperfieldComponents[expr, externals, rules] gives the components of an expression of a superfield, a Grassmann field NambuField_a whose label a = (x, s) stands for a point and a component (the Nambu field NambuField = (psi, psibar), with the antisymmetric propagator (a, b) = -<T NambuField_a NambuField_b>). externals: {label -> component[new label], ...} for every free label ({} for none). rules: field -> {psi, psibar} (required: the superfield and its components, in the order of the component index; e.g. {psiUp, psiDn, psibarUp, psibarDn} with spin); mean -> {Psi, Psibar}; a propagator h -> {G, Gpsipsi, Gpsibarpsibar}, h = [[Gpsipsi, G], [-G^T, Gpsibarpsibar]] with G = -<T psi psibar> and the anomalous propagators Gpsipsi = -<T psi psi>, Gpsibarpsibar = -<T psibar psibar> (heads or 0); any two-label kernel as a matrix h -> {{h11, h12}, {h21, h22}}, h(x s, y t) = h_st(x, y), with entries heads, 0 or functions of two labels (the self-energy {{GapFunctionBar, -Sigma[#2, #1] &}, {Sigma, GapFunction}}: Σ(x psibar, y psi) = Σ(x, y), the gap function Δ(x, y) = Σ(x psibar, y psibar)); a vertex h -> S, its components the derivatives h(a1, ..., ak) = δ/δchi_ak ... δ/δchi_a1 S of the component interaction S. Traces and kernels of operators made of heads without anomalous blocks are written with the normal blocks (Tr ln(-^-1) = 2 Tr ln(-G^-1), Tr(0^-1 .  - 1) = 2 Tr(G0^-1 . G - 1)); with anomalous blocks a trace of products is written as rings (ExpandTrace), while Tr ln of an operator with anomalous blocks has no component form: it is kept as it is, with the message trace, beside the components of the other terms (it does not depend on the means; a derivative of it with respect to a component, G or an anomalous block, gives the message supertrace: take the derivative of the superfield functional with respect to the Nambu propagator first, then its components at zero anomalous blocks). The rule of a mean is mean -> {Psi, Psibar}, e.g. {NambuField -> {psi, psibar}, X -> {Psi, Psibar}, NambuPropagator -> {G, Gpsipsi, Gpsibarpsibar}, BareNambuPropagator -> {G0, 0, 0}, NambuVertex -> S}. The order of the labels of a derivative is the order of the legs: with legs a -> psibar[x1], b -> psi[x2], c -> psibar[x3], d -> psi[x4], FunctionalDerivative[Gamma, X[a], X[b], X[c], X[d]] projects onto FunctionalDerivative[Gamma, Psibar[x1], Psi[x2], Psibar[x3], Psi[x4]], and an odd permutation of the four Grassmann derivatives changes the sign. The result is in canonical form.
